pace.title: Pace
pace.caption: PRs I merged at IPRally each month. 18 in Nov 2025, 182 in Oct 2026: 10× in a year, most of it after the agent pipeline came online.

items.title: Ask AI
items.description: Chat with a patent. Answers cite the exact claim, paragraph or figure — hover to preview, click to jump there. Runs on durable workflows, so long answers survive restarts.

items.title: AI drafting
items.description: Plans and writes a patent application section by section, claims first. Every AI edit arrives as a change you accept or reject, with full version history and undo.

items.title: AI review
items.description: Checks a draft for clarity, claim support and disclosure gaps, and compares claims with prior art. One click applies the suggested fix.

items.title: Figures & files
items.description: Generates and edits patent drawings with reference numbers. Reads uploaded PDFs, Word files and images, and says how much it understood.

items.title: Patent search for agents
items.description: An MCP server that lets Claude run IPRally semantic search and read full patent text.

steps.title: Plan
steps.description: A lead agent reads the ticket and splits it into small units. It never edits code.

steps.title: Build
steps.description: Each unit goes to a worker in its own git worktree. Haiku for chores, Sonnet for clear specs, Opus for open problems.

steps.title: Review
steps.description: Every PR meets three AI reviewers: one for bugs and risk, one adversarial, one for house conventions.

steps.title: Fix
steps.description: A fixer agent answers the findings, repairs red CI and pushes. The loop stops after 8 rounds.

steps.title: Merge
steps.description: I read the diff and merge. No PR goes in unread.

rules.title: House rules for agents
items: Investigate first. Never guess a root cause.
Small PRs. Split anything over ~700 lines.
Run only the tests you touched. Keep loops fast.
One git worktree per task. No force pushes.
Write the why in the commit message.
